reproduction_target: Genome-wide codon usage bias (CUB) analysis across the fungal order Sordariales. Reproduce, from published Sordariales genomes (dataset of Hensen et al. 2023): (1) high-quality CDS filtering; (2) amino-acid frequency, RSCU, GC3, GC12 computation; (3) automatic clustering of genomes by amino-acid composition and RSCU; (4) ancestral-state reconstruction of GC3 over a kingdom-wide fungal phylogeny; (5) ribosomal-gene identification (translate -> InterProScan/Pfam) for a CAI reference set; (6) effective number of codons (ENC) and codon adaptation index (CAI) per genome; (7) neutrality plots (GC12 vs GC3 regression slope) and ENC/GC3 plots to separate selection from mutational bias; (8) family-level statistics (pairwise Wilcoxon + Bonferroni, Pearson correlation, phylogenetically independent contrasts).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool from Methods prose. All steps are computational (W=0; no wet-lab). Repo README + conda-env directory listing read at prose level only (stage-1); scripts NOT read line-by-line. The repo ships conda environment YAMLs (biokit, codonw, r-env, seqtk, fastx, agat) via create-conda-envs.sh claiming to capture 'those versions used in the analysis' -> an env-lock CLAIM (unverified at stage1). README explicitly states blast/bedtools rely on cluster environment-modules NOT included in the conda-envs, so platform coverage is partial. InterProScan is named in Methods but is not present in the conda-env list.

steps.label: High-quality CDS extraction & filtering from annotated Sordariales genomes (custom bash scripts in Genefiltering/): keep spliced CDS with length >=100 bp, no partial codons, no internal stop codons, both start and stop codons
Amino-acid composition, RSCU, GC3 and GC12 per-genome computation with BioKIT V0.1.2 (also used for per-gene GC1/GC2/GC3 in neutrality plots)
Automatic clustering of genomes by amino-acid composition and RSCU with the pheatmap R package
Ancestral-state reconstruction of GC3 over a 689-species kingdom-wide fungal phylogeny (Wint et al. 2022) with phytools V0.6.44 (ContMap function)
Translation of genes for ribosomal-gene identification with seqkit translate
Protein-domain annotation with InterProScan (-appl Pfam) to compile the set of PFAM eukaryotic ribosomal genes used as the CAI reference set
Effective number of codons (ENC) and codon adaptation index (CAI) per genome-wide CDS with CodonW V1.4.2 (-totals setting; correspondence analysis on ribosomal genes as CAI reference)
Neutrality plots: per-gene GC12 vs GC3 regression slope estimation with the ggpubr R package
ENC/GC3 plots (expected-ENC curve, dNC per-gene selection metric) and figure generation with the ggplot2 R package
Phylogenetically independent contrasts to correct trait correlations for phylogenetic dependence with the ape R package
Family-level statistics in R V4.4.1 / RStudio: Shapiro-Wilk normality, pairwise Wilcoxon rank-sum (pairwise.wilcox.test, Bonferroni adjustment), Pearson correlation (cor.test)

headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 10 of 11 computational steps; 1 step (C6, InterProScan) is NI. R★ is not assignable at stage1. This paper IS a stage2 R★ candidate (capture_claim=env_lock_claimed): the repo github.com/NoahH35/CodonUsageBias ships conda-env YAMLs (biokit, codonw, r-env, seqtk, fastx, agat) via create-conda-envs.sh, claimed to pin 'those versions used in the analysis', plus exact prose version pins (BioKIT V0.1.2, phytools V0.6.44, CodonW V1.4.2, R V4.4.1). Upper bound is bounded below full R★ because (a) the env-lock is a stage1 CLAIM only (no conda-lock/container digest verified); (b) README states blast/bedtools rely on cluster environment-modules excluded from the conda-envs (partial platform coverage); (c) InterProScan is not present in the conda-env set; (d) the workflow is explicitly 'not a fully-automated pipeline' and requires manual QC between steps.
headline.coverage: 11 computational steps assessed from Methods prose + repo README + conda-env directory listing (stage1). No wet-lab steps (W=0).

gaps.where: Input genome data (Methods: 'Sequence data collection and filtering')
gaps.missing: No data accession (no GEO/SRA/ENA/Zenodo/figshare) is given in this paper. The genome dataset and phylogeny are attributed to Hensen et al. 2023 ('made available recently', ref 21) and the kingdom-wide phylogeny/GC3 to Wint et al. 2022 (ref 34), via citation only; no per-genome accession list or download manifest is provided here (Table S1 lists species). The README also requires the user to pre-populate Genefiltering/CDS_filtered with per-genome gff+fasta, which are not shipped.
gaps.how_to_close: Provide a versioned accession list / download manifest (or a Zenodo snapshot) mapping each Sordariales genome + outgroup to its source accession, so the input set is reconstructable independently of Hensen et al. 2023.

gaps.missing: Env-lock is a CLAIM only at stage1: conda-env YAMLs (agat, biokit, codonw, fastx, r-env, seqtk) exist but were not verified to pin exact/lockable versions, and no conda-lock/pixi.lock/container digest is present. README explicitly states blast and bedtools rely on cluster environment-modules NOT included in the conda-envs (partial platform coverage). InterProScan (step C6) is named in Methods but absent from the conda-env set and carries no version in prose. seqkit is named in prose while the conda-env ships seqtk (naming mismatch).
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a resolved conda-lock or container digest for a declared platform covering ALL tools (including blast, bedtools, InterProScan), and reconcile the seqkit/seqtk naming.

gaps.missing: README states the scripts 'were not designed to function as a fully-automated pipeline' and are 'a series of individual steps with manual quality control', with intermediate manual copy steps (e.g. copying ribosomal fasta files into CUB_analysis/assemblies/<species>). No single reproducible driver; manual intervention points are not fully specified.
gaps.how_to_close: Provide an end-to-end runnable driver (or document each manual QC/copy step with exact expected inputs/outputs) so the pipeline can be executed deterministically.

gaps.missing: Repo has NO license and NO tagged release / DOI; the paper links a floating HEAD (last push 2025-03-31). No citable commit or archive snapshot is referenced.
gaps.how_to_close: Add an OSI license and mint a tagged release / Zenodo archive with a DOI; cite the exact commit or archive DOI in the paper.
